corridor: FX cross-chain EURX -> SGDX (change reel au pivot d'arrivee par Uniswap V3)

generation.note: Second generation of the corridor contracts. The previous generation (2026-10-14 to 2026-10-17) is kept under "history" and is not replayed. Compliance model of this generation: every check (sanctions, customer due diligence, beneficiary confirmation) is made OFF-CHAIN by each financial institution node, which signs the result; the Policy Wrapper only verifies the proofs carried by the transfer, on-chain, before the wrapped token moves. There is no on-chain identity registry. Since 2026-10-22 the counterparty check is made by a policy that verifies a signed vLEI attestation, not a registry entry (see "vlei" below). Proofs are bound to a leg and a chain, so a proof set travels with the transfer from one chain to the other.

vlei.note: VleiAttestationPolicy (MIT, abi/VleiAttestationPolicy.json) is appended last to the policy lists (transfer and transferFrom) of the source wEURX, where it checks the payer (roles OOR, or agent under a bounded mandate), and of the delivery wSGDX, where it checks the beneficiary (roles OOR or ECR). Before value moves it verifies an EIP-712 attestation signed by a registered off-chain verifier after a KERI/ACDC verification of the party's vLEI presentation and of a two-way wallet binding. The attestation is bound to the transfer (uetr, wallet, asset, chain), is at most 3600 seconds old and is used once; the policy then emits VleiReliedUpon. The pinned root is a TEST root, not GLEIF; the LEIs are fictitious. The chain verifies the verifier's signature, not KERI or ACDC. See references/vlei-gleif.md.

demonstration_passes.note: Live testnet transactions of the demonstration passes of the second generation, played on 2026-10-18 at 1000 EURX between named demonstration financial institutions (FI FR, FI SG1, FI SG2: demonstration labels, not central bank entities). This is data, not a reproducibility claim; it is verified by scripts/demo/corridor-fx-e2e.mjs, which reads each receipt on the public RPC, checks the token movements, the LayerZero guid from the source lock to the arrival, the completed policy runs and the route rule. Refusals made at the source are transactions that REVERT: the script expects EVM status failed, replays each call at the block before to read the error (selector, policy, message) and compare it with the `expected_revert` of the leg, and reads the balances of the payer and of the lock before and after. Refusals made at arrival (the swap is rolled back by the atomic call) succeed at EVM level and carry no token transfer.

Re-applied to the second-generation adapters on 2026-10-18; the library, executor and gas values are unchanged. zk.status: Live. Groth16 (BN254) non-membership proofs of the public sanctions list SAN01 (demonstration list, demonstration setup) are verified on-chain by the universal ZK sanctions policy installed on the wrappers. The proof travels in the same attestation array as the signed checks (kind 2, code sanctions-zkp-public); each proof is bound to its leg and its chain.

routes.note: The arrival composer knows two exchange routes, FIXED in the contract. The compose payload is beneficiary(20) ++ minOut(32) ++ route(1) ++ maxOut(32) ++ attestation. minOut and maxOut bound the SGDX delivered: the attestation is bound to that signed range, not to an exact amount. The composer delivers what the pool returned, capped at maxOut, and keeps any surplus above it in base SGDX; the operator can sweep that surplus to a sink fixed at construction. A read-only route agent quotes both routes on the chain and picks the higher SGDX output (tie: direct); the contract only accepts a route identifier, and minOut applies to the final SGDX, so a wrong choice can only make the whole call fail. All three pools hold base tokens, never wrappers; compliance applies to the transfer of the wrapped SGDX. At 1000 EURX the pool drifts with each pass (a few basis points), and the agent rule switches between the direct and the pivot route accordingly.

history.note: Previous generation (2026-10-14 to 2026-10-17, 50 EURX passes, identity-gated wrappers, earlier adapters and composers). Superseded on 2026-10-18; kept as history, not replayed. The contracts remain on the chains.

demonstration_passes.note: Live testnet transactions of the two demonstration passes, replayed on 2026-10-16 AFTER the LayerZero pathway was pinned (see 'wiring'), each between two named demonstration VASPs. This is data, not a reproducibility claim; it is replayed by scripts/demo/corridor-fx-e2e.mjs, which reads each receipt on the public RPC and renders its state.
